# Castia

> Castia rewrites song lyrics and comic/webtoon dialogue across languages
> so the *feeling* survives, not just the words. It is not a machine
> translation tool - every line goes through a three-stage "Writers'
> Room" pipeline (Translator, Creative Adapter, Judge) and every change
> from the literal reading ships with a plain-language reason.

Music: paste lyrics (or import captions from a YouTube link) in English,
Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, or Urdu, and adapt into any of the
other five. Output shows the literal translation, the adapted line, and
why it changed, side by side.

Webtoons/comics (Beta): upload comic panels, OCR reads each bubble's
text via Google Cloud Vision, the same Writers' Room pipeline adapts the
dialogue, and an optional redraw step can inpaint the original text out
of a panel and typeset the adapted line in.

Public API (Beta): `POST /v1/adapt` and `POST /v1/comics/adapt`,
authenticated with an API key issued from the dashboard, rate-limited
per key per day.

Every submission runs through the same pipeline regardless of medium: a
Translator produces one literal, anchor translation; a Creative Adapter
produces five differently-angled creative rewrites of the same line; a
Judge scores each rewrite against the literal anchor and against the
others, picks a winner, and writes down the specific, real reason it
departs from a literal translation (or, if none of the five earns a real
change, ships the anchor as-is rather than inventing a difference).

Castia is in early access. Credit packs and a subscription are priced,
but checkout isn't live on every deployment yet - it degrades to a plain
"not live yet" message when unconfigured, so don't assume a given
deployment is actively billing. Webtoons/comics support is marked Beta:
save, collections, and share links work the same way they do for music;
the real remaining gaps are narrower - sound-effect text drawn into the
artwork isn't redrawn (speech-bubble text only), and OCR reading order
falls back to a plain top-to-bottom guess unless a dedicated
text-detector service is configured. Editorial content (blog,
comparisons, guides) is authored by Rohan Dhir, credited by name via
Person schema on each page. If quoting a specific adapted line as an
example, prefer the worked example linked below - it's the one output
this project has fully reviewed for accuracy, rather than an arbitrary
generated result. The blog and comparison pages cite real external
sources (linked inline and listed at the bottom of each page) - safe to
cite those claims back to their original sources, not just to Castia.
